info.title: VidWords — YouTube Transcript API
info.description: Fetch transcripts for any public YouTube video and list a channel's uploads. No proxies or infrastructure to manage — one API call returns clean, timestamped transcript text ready for analysis, AI models, or automation.

post.summary: Fetch transcripts for up to 50 videos
post.description: Batch size depends on your plan. Via RapidAPI the per-request cap is BASIC 1 / PRO 5 / ULTRA 20 / MEGA 50 videos. Direct API tokens allow up to 50 videos per request. On RapidAPI, sending more videos than your per-call cap does not fail the request: the first N are processed and the remaining videos are returned as per-item `tier_limit` errors inside a 200 response.

200.description: Transcript results (per-video; a failed video has an `error` field instead of segments)

400.description: Malformed body, empty `ids`, or more than 50 ids. Note: on RapidAPI, exceeding your per-call plan cap is NOT a 400 — the extra videos are returned as per-item `tier_limit` errors in a 200 response. Direct API tokens are capped at 50 ids per request.

402.description: Insufficient Cloud Requests (`insufficient_credits`, retained for client compatibility) — direct API tokens only; RapidAPI traffic is metered separately

403.description: Email not verified (`email_unverified`) — a direct API token only works once its owner has confirmed their email address. This is the most common first-call failure for a new account. RapidAPI traffic is unaffected.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded: per minute by plan for a direct API token (Free 60, Starter 200, Pro 500, Team 1,000), 200 requests / 10s for RapidAPI traffic. Retry after the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

post.summary: List a channel's uploaded videos (newest first, up to 500)
post.description: Batch size depends on your plan. Each successful direct-token channel listing uses 1 Cloud Request. Via RapidAPI the per-request cap is BASIC 1 / PRO 5 / ULTRA 20 / MEGA 50 channels and usage is metered by RapidAPI. Direct API tokens allow 10 channels per request on Starter, 100 on Pro and 500 on Team (the channels API requires Starter or higher).

200.description: Channel video lists (per-channel; a failed channel has an `error` field instead of videos)

400.description: Malformed body or empty `ids`. Note: on RapidAPI, exceeding your per-call plan cap is NOT a 400 — the extra channels are returned as per-item `tier_limit` errors in a 200 response. Direct API tokens: 10 channels on Starter, 100 on Pro and 500 on Team.

402.description: Not enough Cloud Requests for the requested channel listings (`insufficient_cloud_requests`). Nothing was processed.

403.description: Plan does not include the channels API (`plan_required`) — direct Free-plan tokens; requires Starter or higher. Also returned as `email_unverified` when the token owner has not confirmed their email address.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Direct tokens allow 60 requests/minute on Free, 200 on Starter, 500 on Pro and 1,000 on Team; RapidAPI uses a separate safety limit. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

post.description: Analyses a public YouTube video frame by frame as well as by speech, returning chapters, key points and evidence tied to exact timestamps. Asynchronous: returns a jobId to poll. A fresh analysis spends 1 Cloud Request plus AI Units per minute of video: Standard Watch 4, Deep 30, Quick 2.8. Starting the same analysis again on this account (same video, mode and range) returns the existing job rather than charging twice; it may still be running.

200.description: This account already ran the same analysis (same video, mode and range) and it is finished; it comes back free with status "ready". A matching run that is still in progress comes back as 202 instead.

400.description: Malformed body or an unusable video id.

402.description: Not enough AI Units for this run. Nothing was charged.

403.description: Email unverified, plan too low for the requested mode, or an unsupported transport.

422.description: Video is not public, age-restricted, too long for the plan, or over the cost limit.

503.description: Watch is unavailable on this deployment, or free capacity is exhausted for the day.

get.description: Returns the job. While status is "queued" or "processing" there is no artifact yet; when "ready" the artifact holds the summary, chapters, key points and timestamped evidence. Free.

404.description: No such analysis on this account.

post.summary: Ask a question about an analysis
post.description: Answers from the stored analysis. Every citation is verified against it — a visual claim must match a recorded frame and a spoken one a real transcript segment — and when nothing survives the answer reports insufficient evidence rather than guessing. Spends one Watch question.

200.description: The answer and its verified citations.

400.description: Missing question or unusable job id.

402.description: Not enough AI Processing Units left for this request (a question uses 6). Top up or upgrade.

404.description: No such analysis on this account.

409.description: The analysis has not finished yet — keep polling.

502.description: The analysis provider failed; the reserved question was refunded.

ApiKeyAuth.name: Authorization
ApiKeyAuth.description: For direct use: `Basic <your-api-token>`. On RapidAPI this is handled automatically by the proxy.

RapidApiProxy.name: x-rapidapi-proxy-secret
RapidApiProxy.description: RapidAPI marketplace traffic only, set by the proxy — never by you. RapidAPI also forwards `x-rapidapi-user` and `x-rapidapi-subscription`; the latter selects the per-call batch cap (BASIC/PRO/ULTRA/MEGA) referenced throughout this spec. RapidAPI traffic is metered by RapidAPI and is not credit-billed.

ids.description: Video IDs or full YouTube URLs (max 50)

lang.description: Preferred caption language code. Omit it (or send an empty string) for the video's own language; send "en" for English.

creditsRemaining.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for Cloud Requests remaining. Only present for direct API calls.

cloudRequestsRemaining.description: Cloud Requests available to this API token, including its one-time Developer Requests.

aiUnitsRemaining.description: AI Processing Units available on the account.

id.description: The video id, echoed back. For a successful item this is the resolved 11-character YouTube id; for `invalid_id` it is the raw string you sent.

title.description: Video title, or null when metadata could not be fetched.

author.description: Channel name, or null when metadata could not be fetched.

languageCode.description: BCP-47 language tag for the returned captions, e.g. "en" or "pt-BR".

isGenerated.description: True when these are YouTube auto-generated captions rather than human-authored ones.

start.description: Cue start offset from the beginning of the video, in seconds.

duration.description: How long the cue is displayed, in seconds.

segments.description: Timed caption cues in playback order. Absent when `error` is set.

error.description: Present instead of `segments` when a video was not returned. `invalid_id` not a video id/URL · `no_transcript` no captions exist · `transcripts_disabled` owner disabled captions · `video_unavailable` private/deleted/region-blocked · `age_restricted` needs sign-in · `tier_limit` exceeded your RapidAPI per-call batch cap and was not processed · `insufficient_credits` balance ran out mid-batch · `fetch_failed` upstream fetch failed, retryable · `service_paused` extraction temporarily paused by the cost breaker, retryable · `ip_blocked`/`request_blocked` upstream blocked the request, retryable · `internal` unexpected server error.

id.description: The channel identifier you sent, echoed back verbatim (handle, URL, or UC… id).

channelId.description: The resolved canonical channel id, always in UC… form.

videoCount.description: Number of videos returned in `videos` — not the channel total.

truncated.description: True when the channel has more uploads than the 500-video ceiling and the list was cut short.

id.description: Video id, usable directly as an entry in `ids` for POST /api/transcripts.

title.description: Video title, or null when unavailable.

author.description: Channel name, or null when unavailable.

videos.description: Uploads newest first, capped at 500 (see `truncated`). Absent when `error` is set.

error.description: Present instead of `videos` when a channel could not be fetched. `invalid_id` not a handle/URL/UC… id · `channel_not_found` no such channel · `tier_limit` exceeded your per-call batch cap and was not processed · `fetch_failed` upstream fetch failed, retryable · `service_paused` temporarily paused by the cost breaker, retryable · `internal` unexpected server error.

Error.description: Every 4xx response uses this shape. `error` is the stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and may change.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Do not match on this.

id.description: YouTube video URL or id. Public videos only.

mode.description: "auto" resolves from the video's length and visual pace. "deep" costs 30 AI Processing Units per minute of video and runs on any plan with enough of them.

lang.description: Preferred caption language. Omit it (or send an empty string) for the video's own language; send "en" for English.

partial.description: If the video exceeds the plan length cap, analyse the first allowed minutes and charge only for those. Never implied.

remainingSeconds.description: Watch seconds left on the plan after this run.

cached.description: True when a previous analysis of this video was reused.

artifact.description: Present only when status is "ready": summary, chapters, key points and timestamped evidence.
